ai.literal: Among wealth, wealth is ear-wealth; that wealth among wealth all is head.
ai.translation: The finest wealth among all wealth is the wealth of hearing. That wealth is the chief of all riches.
ai.modern: செல்வங்களில் சிறந்த செல்வம் செவியால் கேட்டுப் பெறும் செல்வமே ஆகும். அந்தச் செல்வம் மற்ற எல்லாச் செல்வங்களிலும் முதன்மையானதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the supreme value of listening and learning. It calls the knowledge gained through the ear the greatest of all riches. While material wealth can be lost or stolen, the wealth of hearing remains secure and enriches the mind. Therefore, it stands as the head or chief among all types of wealth a person can possess.

ai.literal: To the ear food not having time, a little to the stomach also will be given.
ai.translation: When there is no food for the ear, a little may be given to the stomach as well.
ai.modern: செவிக்கு அறிவாகிய உணவு கிடைக்காத போது, உடலை வளர்க்கும் வயிற்றுக்கும் சிறிது உணவு தரப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the nourishment of the mind with the nourishment of the body. The phrase 'food for the ear' refers to learning and listening to wisdom, which is presented as the primary human need. Only when there is no opportunity to feed the ear should one provide a little food to the stomach. The suffix 'um' (also/even) attached to the stomach emphasizes that physical hunger is strictly secondary to intellectual growth.

ai.literal: Ear's food-having listening those-who-possess, oblation food-having exalted-ones-with are-equal earth-on.
ai.translation: Those who possess the learning that feeds the ear are equal on earth to the exalted gods who feed on sacrificial offerings.
ai.modern: செவிக்கு உணவாகிய கேள்வியினை உடையவர்கள், இந்த நிலவுலகத்தில் வாழ்ந்தாலும், வேள்வியில் தரப்படும் அவியுணவை உண்ணும் தேவர்களுக்கு ஒப்பானவர்கள் ஆவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the pursuit of knowledge through listening to the divine nourishment of the gods. The word 'கேள்வி' (listening or learning) is described as 'செவியுணவு' (food for the ear). Those who sustain themselves with this intellectual nourishment are said to be equal ('ஒப்பர்') to the exalted beings ('ஆன்றார்') who consume sacrificial offerings ('அவி'). Thus, acquiring wisdom through hearing elevates ordinary humans on earth to a divine status.

ai.literal: He has not learned, even if, let him listen; that, to one, in weakness, a prop becoming help.
ai.translation: Even if one lacks learning, let him listen to the wise. In times of weakness, that will be a supporting prop.
ai.modern: ஒருவன் நூல்களைக் கற்கவில்லை என்றாலும், கற்றவரிடம் கேட்டு அறிய வேண்டும். அது அவனுக்குத் தளர்ச்சி வரும் காலத்தில் ஊன்றுகோல் போலத் துணையாக இருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the value of listening to the wise, even if one lacks formal education. The word 'ஒற்கம்' refers to a state of weakness, adversity, or faltering. In such difficult times, the knowledge gained through listening acts as an 'ஊற்று' (a prop or walking stick), providing steady support. Thus, auditory learning serves as a reliable guide when one's own understanding might stumble.

ai.literal: slipping where-there-is support-stick like-indeed good-conduct those-who-possess mouth word
ai.translation: The words from the mouths of those with good conduct are like a supporting staff on slippery ground.
ai.modern: வழுக்கும் நிலத்தில் நடக்கும்போது ஊன்றுகோல் எப்படி உதவுமோ, அதுபோலவே நல்லொழுக்கம் உடையவர்களின் வாயிலிருந்து வரும் சொற்கள் ஒருவருக்குத் துணையாக இருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the words of virtuous people to a walking stick used on slippery ground. Just as a staff prevents a person from falling when the path is treacherous, the advice of those with good conduct keeps a person from moral or practical failure. The word 'ஊற்றுக்கோல்' vividly captures this idea of firm support in times of instability.

ai.literal: However small even, good things let one listen; that much even, excellent greatness it will give.
ai.translation: Let one listen to good things, however small they may be; even that much will bring them excellent greatness.
ai.modern: எவ்வளவு சிறியதாக இருந்தாலும் நல்ல விஷயங்களைக் கேட்க வேண்டும்; அது அந்த அளவிற்கு நிறைந்த பெருமையைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the value of listening to good and virtuous teachings. The word 'எனைத்தானும்' suggests that no piece of good advice is too insignificant to hear. 'அனைத்தானும்' promises a proportional reward, showing that every little bit of wisdom accumulates. Ultimately, such listening yields 'ஆன்ற பெருமை', elevating the listener's character and dignity.

ai.literal: Having erred even if understood, foolishness they will not say, having examined minutely and understood, accumulated learning-by-hearing they.
ai.translation: Even if they have misunderstood something by mistake, those who have accumulated learning through subtle examination and understanding will not speak foolish words.
ai.modern: நுட்பமாக ஆராய்ந்து உணர்ந்து பெற்ற கேள்வியறிவை உடையவர்கள், ஒருவேளை தவறாகப் புரிந்து கொண்டிருந்தாலும், பேதைமையான சொற்களைச் சொல்ல மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the maturity of those who have gained deep knowledge through attentive listening. The phrase 'இழைத்து உணர்ந்து ஈண்டிய கேள்வி' refers to learning that is accumulated by minutely examining and truly understanding what is heard. Because their foundation is so thorough, even if they happen to misunderstand a specific point ('பிழைத்து உணர்ந்தும்'), they will restrain themselves and not blurt out foolish or ignorant words ('பேதைமை சொல்லார்'). Their deep learning gives them the wisdom to avoid speaking rashly.

ai.literal: Even if they hear, not hearing of the nature indeed, by instruction to be pierced which are not ears.
ai.translation: Ears that have not been pierced by listening to instruction are effectively deaf, even if they can physically hear.
ai.modern: அறிவுரைகளைக் கேட்டுத் துளைக்கப்படாத காதுகள், ஒலியைக் கேட்கும் திறன் பெற்றிருந்தாலும், அவை செவிடான காதுகளின் தன்மையையே உடையனவாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts physical hearing with intellectual listening. The poet states that ears not opened or pierced by profound instruction might as well be deaf. Even if such ears physically perceive sound, they possess the nature of unhearing ears because they fail to absorb wisdom. The striking metaphor of piercing the ear with knowledge emphasizes that true hearing requires active, receptive learning.

ai.literal: Those who are not people of subtle hearing, becoming people of humble mouth is rare.
ai.translation: It is rare for those without subtle learning to speak with humble words.
ai.modern: நுட்பமான கேள்வியறிவு இல்லாதவர்கள் பணிவான சொற்களைப் பேசுபவர்களாக ஆவது கடினம்.
ai.explanation: This couplet connects the depth of one's listening to the humility of one's speech. The word 'நுணங்கிய' (subtle or refined) describes the quality of learning acquired through careful hearing. Those who lack this refined understanding rarely possess a 'வணங்கிய வாய்' (a bowed or humble mouth). True learning naturally brings modesty to a person's words, while the absence of deep listening results in arrogant or unrefined speech.

ai.literal: In the ear taste who do not perceive, mouth possessing perception base people, even if they perish even if they live, what?
ai.translation: What does it matter whether those base people live or die, who know only the taste of the mouth and not the taste of the ear?
ai.modern: செவியால் அறியும் கேள்வியின் சுவையை உணராமல், வாயால் அறியும் உணவின் சுவையை மட்டுமே உணரும் மனிதர்கள் வாழ்ந்தால் என்ன, இறந்தால் என்ன?
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the intellectual pleasure of listening with the physical pleasure of eating. The phrase 'செவியில் சுவை உணரா' refers to those who do not appreciate the taste of knowledge gained through the ear. They are described as 'வாய் உணர்வின் மாக்கள்', base people who only understand the taste of the mouth. The poet asks what difference it makes whether such unrefined individuals live or die, as their existence contributes nothing of higher value to the world.
